summary: Brick and granite light off the northeast end of Cape Ann, first lit 1835; the 1896 tower stands on the 1851 stone tower's foundation. Owned by Rockport; island is a bird sanctuary.

structures.note: Cylindrical brick tower, 37 ft to the center of the lantern; set on the foundation of the 1851 tower (LighthouseFriends).
Octagonal stone tower on the northeastern tip, 24 ft; construction began in 1851. The single source is LighthouseFriends.
First brick tower, 19 ft (LighthouseFriends); the nomination dates a brick tower to 1835.
Six-room, one-and-a-half-story wood-frame house in Gothic style. The archive gives 1878; the nomination dates the Gothic house to 1835.
LighthouseFriends dates the oil house to 1905. The nomination lists an 1835 stone oil house and describes the present building as brick.

access.note: Island is private (Massachusetts Audubon bird sanctuary). The archive lists the station as not open to the public; LighthouseFriends describes summer association trips to the island.

facts.agency: Town of Rockport (owner of the light); Thacher Island Town Committee (manager); Massachusetts Audubon Society (owner of the island)

events.note: Site sold to the federal government by Aaron and Solomon Poole for $600 (28 November 1834).
Construction began on a new octagonal stone tower on the northeastern tip (LighthouseFriends only).
Sixth-order Fresnel lens received (archive record; LighthouseFriends).
Footbridge from dwelling to tower rebuilt.
Light shown from a temporary tower from May 1896; moved into the new brick tower on 30 July 1896.
About 120 running feet of stone and gravel walk laid; boathouse moved onto stone piers.
Changed from white to green, flashing every six seconds.
Island except the 1.8-acre light station sold to Glenn Wilson of New York for $3,050.
Archive date. LighthouseFriends says the light was automated in the early 1930s; see notes.
Electric foghorn installed on the active tower.
Tower painted; new windows and door installed.
Entry house to the tower destroyed in the October 1991 storm (LighthouseFriends).
Coast Guard handed the light and its 1.8 acres to the Town of Rockport, 16 July 2010.
Restoration of the lighthouse and keeper's house completed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1835 date is for the first tower and keeper's house. The first tower was replaced; the standing tower dates from 1896 (archive; Light-House Board report for fiscal 1897). LighthouseFriends places a stone tower on the northeastern tip between them, in 1851, a date the nomination and archive do not give.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved conflicts, none settled in the story. (1) Automation: the archive gives 1967 and the record says automated; LighthouseFriends says early 1930s, when a local man was licensed to live in the keeper's dwelling. The archive roster ends with Hoyt P. Smith in 1933. (2) Keeper's dwelling: the nomination dates the surviving Gothic house to 1835; LighthouseFriends says a new house was finished in 1877; the archive says 1878. (3) Oil house: nomination says 1835 stone oil house and describes a brick building; LighthouseFriends says 1905. (4) The 1835-1851 history (the 1842 Lewis inspection, the 1843 Davis letter, the 1851 stone tower on the northeastern tip, the 1857 lens) rests on LighthouseFriends alone. The Light-House Board's earlier annual reports are not in the local corpus (it starts in 1891), and the nomination and archive do not mention an 1851 tower. The story attributes these to LighthouseFriends. (5) The LighthouseFriends page prints the 1834 appropriation spend as '$4.091.29'; the story uses $4,091.29. (6) The first keeper's second stint is listed as Benjamin W. Andrews in the archive and as Benjamin W. Andrews, Jr. by LighthouseFriends; the person slugs are the archive's. (7) The Life-Saving Service station: the 1900 table lists Gap Cove, one-half mile west of Straitsmouth light; the 1909 report refers to 'the Straitsmouth life-saving station'. These are probably the same station, but no source says so. No record for that station exists in data/stations/ma. (8) The 1902 Life-Saving Service casualty table (data/raw/corpus/lss/1902) has a vessel 'stranded on N. side of Straitsmouth Island' at 9.30 a.m.; the OCR column layout did not let us match its date with confidence, so it is left out. (9) Newspapers: Chronicling America returned HTTP 520 errors for the keeper and station searches; the one 'Straitsmouth Island' search that ran returned four unrelated Massachusetts pages. No newspaper source is used. (10) Wikipedia was read only for leads. It gives an NRHP listing date of 15 June 1987 that no source we read confirmed, so no nrhp_listed event is entered. (11) Visiting arrangements (association trips on Tuesdays) come from a LighthouseFriends page that may be out of date; check before publishing. (12) The record's range (6 nm) and the lens status are not in any source read; omitted from facts. (13) The 1960 occupant is deliberately not named; he is a private person. No other_stations links are asserted. (14) Fact-check 2026-10-22: the NRHP form (Lighthouse Information Form 37, dated July 1981) lists the lighthouse as '(1835)' in its major elements and describes a 'white cylindrical tower 37" high', while its chronology gives 1835 for the brick tower and the archive, LighthouseFriends and the Light-House Board (fiscal 1896 'rebuilt on the same foundations', scan p.58) date the standing tower to 1896. The story states the disagreement in its opening. (15) LighthouseFriends prints the appropriation spend as '$4.091.29'; the story uses $4,091.29. (16) The 1851 tower: LighthouseFriends says construction began in 1851, not that the tower was finished that year; the story says so. (17) The 1909 casualty narrative (scan p.50) names the Straitsmouth station only as the station within whose official jurisdiction the casualty happened; the place of the casualty is not given, so the story does not say 'near Rockport'. (18) The 1960 occupant was the stepson of the later owner (William Francis Gibbs, per LighthouseFriends). Neither man is named in the story; the stepson is a private person. (19) Oil house: the Board's fiscal 1894 'brick oil house was built' sentence (scan p.357) belongs to the entry before Straitsmouth (no. 73), not to Straitsmouth. (20) Fiscal years checked against scan positions: the FY1894 report starts at scan p.302 of annualreportlig01statgoog; the FY1896 and FY1897 entries are in annualreportlig02statgoog (FY1897 at scan p.266 onward); the FY1900 entry is at scan p.57 of annualreportlig00statgoog. (21) OCR table matched by position: the Gap Cove row of the 1900 Life-Saving Service station table (scan p.316 of lifesavingservic17unitrich: "Gap Cove Mass One-half mile west of Straitsmouth light 42 39 30 70 36 00") was read from the OCR text, not the page image. The 1902 table (scan p.340 of lifesavingservic15unitrich) repeats the same coordinates against "One-half of a mile west of Straitsmouth light". The checker should view scan p.316 to confirm the name and the distance sit in the same row.
